note: Every entry carries both `id` and `finding` with the same value: the record shape asked for by the orchestrator names the field `id`, and tools/check_ceremony.py reads `finding`.
method: Rule applied to every restate-and-extend finding (R60B-004 to R60B-011), row by row, with the orchestrator's test as the arbiter - a sourced row's quote must support the whole row. Where the post-marker clause asserts a mechanism or an obligation the quote cannot carry, the clause was split into its own origin=proposed row (with the research query the proposed convention requires) or, where the row's whole point was that clause, the row itself was converted to origin=proposed with the restatement reduced to a one-clause pointer. Where the clause only re-explained the row's own action, it was deleted. Where the quote does support the clause, the row stayed sourced and the 'X already states ... What this adds' scaffolding was replaced by a one-clause owner pointer, so the row reads as one claim under its own quote; 'already states' and 'what this adds' were dropped because those phrases are what the checker keys on, and the owner is still named so no compose-by-name warning appears (the same remedy ceremony 59 recorded in R59A-009). No row was resolved by inserting the word 'proposed' into a sourced row: that clears the warning while leaving the extension riding on someone else's quote.

lessons_for_next_section: The restate-and-extend backlog is not one defect but three: a clause the quote does support (fix by dropping the 'already states / what this adds' scaffolding and naming the owner once), a clause that states a mechanism or obligation of this skill's own (fix by splitting it into an origin=proposed row), and a clause that repeats the row's own action (fix by deleting it). Sorting the rows into those three buckets first made 30 flagged rows a mechanical pass.

Section budgets decide where a split lands. Instructions cap at 10 and invariants at 10, so in cap-isolation, cap-mandate-broker and cap-model-access the extension had to move to best practices or be deleted; an improver who splits in place hits the budget warning and trades one warning for another.

tools/validate_skills.py reads a row's prose from a fixed field list that does not include a shapes row's `name`, so a shape can never clear a compose-by-name warning by naming its owner. Re-anchoring the row on a quote of its own is the only fix, and the pointer is still worth writing for the reader.
